catalyst_3.evidence: Near-kill resolved IN the line's favor: the DEFM14A (filed 2026-08-24) contains a $3.75/sh July 15 Dividend (record 2026-06-30, PAID 2026-07-15) — if the $7.75-8.50 had been inclusive of it, remaining value would be $4.00-4.75 vs a $6.88 price and the line would be dead. Primary-source confirmations: vote "September 29, 2026, at 10:00 a.m., Eastern Time"; initial distribution "between $3.70 and $4.00 per Share" "within approximately 30 days following stockholder approval"; "$7.75 and $8.50 per Share... assuming a complete liquidation by the first half of 2028"; post-sale balance sheet "$1.3 billion of cash, $0.9 billion in real estate owned... $0.4 billion in debt"; trust interests "will not be transferable." NUMERATOR RE-DERIVED bottom-up rather than inherited: 1300 + 900 - 400 = $1,800M, less $491M dividend paid and $172.5M preferred = $1,136M / 131.0M sh = $8.67/sh pre-wind-down-costs, bracketing the range from above — attack (6) fails. ALREADY-HARVESTED (attack 7) FAILS DECISIVELY on the tape: pre-Athene base 2026-01-27 = $10.12 vs today's dividend-adjusted $10.63 ($6.88 + $3.75) = +5.0% in seven months, and the 2026-06-16 plan announcement moved it only $10.66 -> $10.83 (+1.6%). No re-rate; genuinely unpriced. CORRECTIONS: (a) proxy BVPS is $12.15 post-preferred PRE-dividend, not $8.44 — the ~$8.40 post-dividend figure is a derivation, not a quoted line; (b) the near cash is ~56% of price but only ~47% of remaining value, so "over half" overstates the fast leg; (c) the retained $0.9B is foreclosed REAL ESTATE OWNED carrying $0.4B of debt, and ARI is EXTERNALLY MANAGED — Apollo collects fees on those assets through a two-year wind-down, a drag the line omits whose incentive does not favor speed; a 20% REO markdown is ~$1.37/sh and alone would push the midpoint below today's price. Score trimmed 7 -> 6.5: event and discount are real and verified, but roughly half the payoff sits behind a non-transferable, delisted, fee-dragged trust stub whose implied +24-58% over ~18mo is rational illiquidity compensation rather than clean mispricing.

catalyst_3.title: Verify
catalyst_3.evidence: FORWARD is NOT the statistically significant Phase 3 - it is an open-label US/EU generalizability bridge, and that bridge is the reason the BLA slipped a full year. The stat-sig pivotal was the 2024 Bangladesh/Philippines Phase 3 (ANX005 30mg/kg, 2.4x GBS-DS improvement at Wk8, p=0.0058; the 75mg/kg arm MISSED). Annexon guided a BLA off that data for 2025; FDA instead required a "generalizability package," pushing submission to Q4-2026 with FORWARD (early data = first 10 patients, open-label) as the supporting set. So the BLA is not a mechanical filing off a clean pivotal - it rests on an FDA-negotiated bridge from a non-Western population that has already caused one 12-month slip, and the same agency posture can slip it again past Q4. Second correction: net cash is ~$159M, not $175M - $209.2M cash/ST investments at 6/30/26 LESS $50M already DRAWN on the $200M Oxford facility; that is senior secured debt sitting ahead of the common, so "no preferred, clean waterfall" is right in kind but overstated ~10% and omits the drawn tranche. Against ~$55M/qtr net loss ($55.3M Q2, $0.28/sh) the cash column is ~3 quarters, which is precisely why the ATM keeps running into the print. What SURVIVES intact: both events are real, company-guided, dated and fully forward (Month-15 ARCHER II primary "on track for Q4 2026," Month-24 dual primary ADDED while retaining Month-15, completion Q3-2027; BLA "expected in Q4 2026"; EU MAA submitted 2026-01-08 and confirmed still under review at the 8/12 Q2 release). The already-harvested test passes decisively and has strengthened since the line was written: ANNX trades $4.87, BELOW both the 50d ($5.38) and 200d ($5.39) averages, 32% under the $7.18 52wk high, and down another 7.4% from the $5.26 8/12 print the line cited - the catalysts have been public since January and the tape has faded them, not paid them. EV recomputes to ~$639M (163.8M shares x $4.87 = $798M cap, less $209M cash, plus $50M debt), close enough to the line's $623M that the "ARCHER II carried at zero" framing holds. Net: thesis stands, two load-bearing facts wrong, and the BLA's regulatory certainty is materially lower than "off a statistically significant Phase 3" implies - trim 7 to 6.

catalyst_3.evidence: The "unpriced hard gate" framing is wrong in direction: the gate is priced and being repriced ADVERSELY. Delaware Commissioner Navarro's own 2026-08-17 department release states no public hearing has been scheduled and that "no inference should be drawn regarding the current stage of the review," while confirming the department has retained outside actuaries, valuation experts, financial advisors, auditors and accountants to vet Aquarian — i.e. a deep look at the buyer's balance sheet with no clock. catalyst_3.title: Verify
catalyst_3.evidence: STARBOARD "CONTROL" IS FALSE AND THE PROCEEDS ARE NOT EARMARKED FOR HOLDERS. Line claims "Starboard holding 4 of 10 board seats to force the proceeds toward capital return." Primary (3/23/26 cooperation agreement, 8-K ex99.1): board expanded 8->10; only TWO directors seated immediately (Dhiren Fonseca, Andrew Cates - independent industry figures, not Starboard partners), two more merely RECOMMENDED at the 2026 annual meeting; and Starboard signed a STANDSTILL agreeing not to nominate a slate and to vote all its shares FOR management's nominees. That is a minority, standstill-bound, largely-independent bloc - not a mechanism to "force" anything. Compounding it, the company's own 6/15/26 release names the uses of proceeds as "share repurchases, debt paydown, or inorganic investment within the experiences category" - the exact reinvestment/growth language that lets proceeds never reach the common. No dollar-sized buyback authorization exists and ZERO repurchases occurred in Q2 (the company instead repaid $345.0M of 2026 Senior Notes, evidencing revealed preference for debt paydown over buyback). Second correction: the put is no longer an unexercised option - French works council concluded 7/30/26, TRIP exercised, and a DEFINITIVE Equity Purchase Agreement was signed 8/2/26 (this cuts in the thesis's favor; the deal is more committed than described). WHAT SURVIVES, cleanly: $700M all-cash, closing by YE2026; numerator provenance PASSES verbatim - "anticipates minimal tax cost... net proceeds expected to closely approximate the gross proceeds"; waterfall clean per 6/30/26 balance sheet - preferredStock $0, minorityInterest $0, no PIK stack, no external manager; 25x multiple correct ($700M / $28M TheFork LTM adj EBITDA); net debt $50.7M + $700M = ~$649M net cash vs $1.085B cap => ~$436M stub EV, arithmetic confirmed. ALREADY-HARVESTED test passes decisively and is the strongest leg: $9.325 vs 52wk low $9.01 (3.5% above the LOW) and 52wk high $20.16, ~24% BELOW the 50d avg $12.35 - the stock is lower than pre-announcement, so none of the payoff was captured. Residual intact. But the reason it's cheap is real and is the score cap: continuing-ops Q2 revenue -7% y/y, Hotels -23%, media -12%, adj EBITDA $76.4M -21% y/y on AI-search disintermediation. The cash is near-certain; the stub is a melting asset and the capital-return size remains uncommitted until Q3 earnings.

catalyst_3.title: Verify
catalyst_3.evidence: The flag's two differentiating claims are both false. (1) "G1 never fired - no counterparty, price or LOI has been named": WRONG. American Industrial Partners proposed $11-12/share CASH on 2025-11-18 (to combine RYAM with its portfolio co Global Cellulose Fibers); the board REJECTED it by letter 2025-12-18; the rejection was made public late Feb 2026 via a Schedule 13D (Mill Pond Capital activism, AIP 13D also on file), and AIP stated it remains open to participate. The counterparty, the price and the rejection are all named and on the SEC record. (2) "literally zero harvest": WRONG. RYAM closed $7.17 on 2026-02-24 and $10.23 on 2026-02-25 - a +42.7% one-day re-rate on that disclosure - and ran to $11.75 on 2026-03-17 (52wk high $11.85), i.e. it already TOUCHED the AIP bid range and the top of the modeled value, then round-tripped. The announcement re-rate was harvested in February; only the give-back makes today look cheap. The -16.7% vs the 2026-04-17 close of $10.21 is arithmetically right ($8.50/$10.21) but is measured off a post-pop base, not a pre-catalyst base. Numerator is also overstated: 8.5-9.0x the $173M covenant EBITDA (= $726M net secured / 4.2x, both confirmed in the 8-K Q2 exhibit) less $755M adj. net debt over 67.5M shares yields $10.60-11.88, NOT $10.60-13.55 ($13.55 needs 9.65x). Honest band ~$10.6-12.0 (which is exactly AIP's rejected $11-12), so upside is +25% to +41% against a $5.38 no-deal low = ~1:1 reward/risk, not the claimed 1.6:1. CONFIRMED and unchanged: 2026-04-20 board-run review, Morgan Stanley + Wachtell Lipton, scope incl. continuation of standalone plan, Q4-2026 "clear path forward" reaffirmed in the 2026-08-04 Q2 release; NO preferred stock ahead of the common (waterfall is clean, unlike FIP); Paperboard/High-Yield Pulp 1H adj. EBITDA -$15M with a $13M Q2 impairment; $145M liquidity. Flag also omits that a permanent CEO with transaction experience (Daniel M. Krawczyk) has been seated since the 2026-08-04 release - a fact that cuts FOR the thesis. Net: real, live, dated, unfired process with a genuine arms-length numerator, but the board already rejected the price that defines that numerator, the market has since voted no-deal by fading the stock 29% below it, and the setup is a ~1:1 levered stub - not the clean residual the flag describes.

valuation.valuation_basis: Single FORWARD binary: opakalim/BHV-7000 (selective Kv7.2/7.3 activator) topline from the FIRST of TWO pivotal Ph2/3 refractory-focal-epilepsy studies, 2H-2026. Supportive prior data: 54% achieved >=50% seizure reduction over 6mo, triple time-to-seizure, low CNS-AE / differentiated tolerability (>1000 subjects). Textbook single-readout-without-clear-mispricing: won't register on one study, and epilepsy adjunctive trials carry placebo-response variance. Cash $351.8M (3/31/26) / 105.865M sh = $3.32/sh — but BHVN retains multiple shots (Graves', IgAN, SMA-adjacent) so a miss does NOT cut to cash. win_prob 0.55 = Kv7 mechanism clinically validated (ezogabine precedent) + strong Ph2 effect, discounted for single-study + placebo risk + need to confirm in study 2. target_on_win $18 ~ FMP consensus median $18 (cons $17.6); downside_on_loss $6 (re-rates down hard but residual pipeline+cash floor >$3.32 cash). EV barbell: 0.55*(18-11.18)+0.45*(6-11.18)= +$1.42/sh (~+13% EV, but high variance). reference_rr (EV%)=(18-11.18)/(11.18-6)=1.32.
valuation.prob_basis: Kv7.2/7.3 mechanism de-risked by ezogabine/retigabine precedent + opakalim Ph2 efficacy (54% >=50% responders, well tolerated). Capped at 0.55 because this is FIRST of two registration studies (no filing on a single readout) and adjunctive focal-epilepsy placebo response is a known confounder.

But note asymmetry: at $139 the stock already prices most of the win (49% upside to $208) vs ~57% downside to $60. EV barbell: 0.78*(208-139.31)+0.22*(60-139.31)= +$36.1/sh (~+26% EV). reference_rr=(208-139.31)/(139.31-60)=0.87.
valuation.prob_basis: Positive pivotal Ph3 DRAGON (met primary, ~36% lesion-growth reduction, clean safety) + Breakthrough/Fast Track/RPD/Orphan designations de-risk the approval path; discounted from ~0.85 for single-pivotal adequacy in a first-ever-approved indication and CMC/rolling-review execution.

catalyst_3.title: Verify
catalyst_3.evidence: PRIMARY-SOURCE CHECK (8-K filed 2026-08-24, SEC Accession 0001193125-26-363681): the core facts hold — Hub Group is out of compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5250(c)(1), received "a 180-day exception period, or until September 14, 2026," to file the delinquent FY2025 10-K and Q1 2026 10-Q (Q2 10-Q also delinquent, NT 10-Q filed 2026-08-11), and as of 2026-09-06 EDGAR shows NO 10-K, NO 10-Q and no 8-K after 08-24, so the catalyst is genuinely unfired 8 days out. Price/harvest check also holds: $36.68 vs $53.26 52wk high, 50d avg $44.24, 52wk low $32.90 — the stock de-rated INTO the date, so nothing is pre-captured. BUT the load-bearing framing word is FALSE. "Non-extendable ... delisting" is wrong: under Nasdaq Rule 5810(c)(2)/5815, 180 days is the maximum the STAFF may grant, not the maximum the company may remain listed. A miss on 09-14 produces a Staff Delisting Determination that the company can appeal to a Hearings Panel; the appeal STAYS suspension and the Panel may keep the security listed up to 360 calendar days from the original filing due date (~2026-03-17 → ~2027-03-12). So 09-14 is not a cliff, it is a checkpoint — which guts the asymmetry the thesis is built on in both directions: there is no forced-delisting downside to be relieved, and therefore no mechanical reason a "delisting discount" must close that day. Second correction: the numerator has no provenance. The waterfall IS clean (zero preferred, no PIK, no external manager — that part is correct and re-derived), but the "+20% to a $44 pre-deadline base" is simply the 50-day moving average used as a price anchor; nothing ties the ~$1.0B of market-cap loss to the listing status rather than to the 2026-05-11 fraud disclosure ($77M understated purchased transportation, 3-year class period 2023-04-28 to 2026-05-11), a departed CFO and COO (both left 2026-05-27, interim CFO on a $125k/month consulting deal), and a weak intermodal tape. Third: the event is two-sided information release, not discount removal — a clean 09-14 file dumps restated FY23-25, Q1 and Q2 2026 numbers plus an adverse ICFR opinion simultaneously, and the stated restatement scope could not be confirmed as still $77M. Real, cheap, unfired, correctly dated — but the "binary, mechanical, non-extendable" premise that justified a 6 does not survive the rule text.

catalyst_3.title: Verify
catalyst_3.evidence: The line's single strongest argument — "MGM has fully round-tripped and trades 5.6% BELOW its undisturbed pre-bid close, so the spread is genuinely unharvested" — is computed off a CONTAMINATED base. $43.67 (Fri 2026-05-29) was not undisturbed: MGM ran +13.6% in the three sessions into it (5/26 $38.45 -> 5/27 $41.95 on 10.05M shares vs ~4-6M normal -> 5/28 $42.93 -> 5/29 $43.67) on leaked deal-talk reports. People Inc.'s own 6/1 release prices the offer as only a 10.6% premium to that 5/29 close but a 24.1% premium to the 30-day VWAP ending 5/29 (implied VWAP ~$38.92) and >30% to the 90-day VWAP. Against the true undisturbed base MGM at $41.22 is roughly +6% ABOVE, not -5.6% below — about a quarter of the offered premium is already in the tape, and 41.22 sits only ~4% over the 200d MA of $39.59. The residual-capture test still passes directionally (the full announcement pop $50.69 -> $41.22 has been given back) but far more weakly than the case claims, and it was the stated reason the score was held at 6. Second correction: the proposal is dated 2026-06-01, not 2026-07-30 (that is the special-committee disclosure date on the Q2 call). Third, the write-up omits live BIDDER-ABANDONMENT risk: Bloomberg 2026-08-03 reported a People Inc. shareholder publicly urging it to DROP the MGM bid and redirect capital to buybacks, and People's own release says it expects to fund with cash at People AND AT MGM plus "additional debt and equity funding commitments" — i.e. uncommitted, partly target-funded (CreditSights flagged debt funding as the key uncertainty). Everything else verifies: live unsolicited all-cash $48.30/sh for the 73.9% People does not own (26.1% held), ~$12.4B equity / ~$18B EV, independent committee with its own outside advisers, no signed agreement, no disclosed deadline, MGM $41.22 (52wk 29.19-51.59, so no 52wk-high disqualifier), gross spread 17.2%. Numerator provenance is clean — $48.30 is the bidder's own stated cash price, not an inherited analyst target or an unwaterfalled SoP.

valuation.valuation_basis: Minority-squeeze merger-arb, all-cash but PRE-AGREEMENT. People Inc. (formerly IAC; 26.1% holder via Barry Diller) tabled a NON-BINDING $48.30/share all-cash proposal Jun 1 2026 (~$18B incl. debt) to take the remaining 73.9% private; 24.1% premium to 30-day VWAP, 10.6% premium to the prior close. Board confirmed receipt Jun 1 and is reviewing with advisors -> no signed agreement, no price certainty. deal_price=$48.30; undisturbed=$43.67 ($48.30/1.106, last close before the bid). At live $47.21 the stock already sits ~98% of the headline bid (a sell-side analyst argues the board should demand more), so the spread is thin and skewed: limited arb capture to $48.30, an embedded BUMP option above it, against a real no-deal/standalone reversion to ~$43.67. Elevated break_prob reflects the non-binding status, controller-conflict process, and gaming/regulatory licensing approvals.

Dow final investment decision explicitly NOT expected before 2028. | The triage read the tape correctly but mis-assigned the lane: the overhang event it names — the Sept-1-2026 IPO lockup expiry — has already FIRED, six days ago, so what is being underwritten is a 4-8 week absorption forecast rather than a dated forward catalyst, and absorption clears no Bloom gate. The genuinely unfired item, the NRC final safety evaluation and construction permit for Long Mott, is real, well-dated (Nov-2026 target under the EO 14300 clock, draft SE done and environmental review closed with a FONSI) and has a named counterparty in Dow — but it fails G2 and G3 hard: Dow is on record that its final investment decision is not expected before 2028, so permit issuance commits no capital and produces no re-derivable figure to price against today's $17.71. On numerator provenance the equity itself is cleaner than feared — the $2.34B preferred stack converted at the IPO, there is no debt, and ~$1.9B of cash and investments against ~280M diluted shares gives a ~$6.8/sh net-cash anchor and ~4 years of runway — but with Q2 revenue of $54.6M carrying a negative gross margin, the residual ~$3.1B of EV is a thematic SMR/AI-power bet, which is the excluded category. The one honest positive is that nothing is harvested: at -23% from the IPO price and -52% off the high, this is an early-arc suppressed underlying with zero run-up, so it earns a WATCH — but per the score-the-equity-not-the-event rule the score caps at 4, and it should only escalate if a permit grant is paired with a dated, named, dollar-quantified Dow or third-party commitment rather than the 2028 FID placeholder.

candidates.instrument: common units (NYSE: XIFR), $12.14 as of 2026-09-06 close
candidates.analysis_summary: [MILESTONE] Q3 2026 results (expected late Oct 2026, following the 2026-07-28 Q2 filing) is the next hard date; the substantive milestones are the next CEPF 5 buyout window "sometime in 2027" (~$470m planned) and the refinancing of corporate notes maturing 2027, targeted "early part of 2027" — year-level windows, not dates. | NUMERATOR PROVENANCE (re-derived, not inherited): at 6/30/2026 XIFR carries $6.03bn total debt, $500m cash and — critically — $7.373bn of third-party non-controlling equity (CEPF plus tax equity) structurally ahead of a $1.144bn common market cap; NCI has run off only $336m in six months ($7.709bn at 12/31/2025 to $7.373bn), so the ">$2bn by 2030" plan consumes essentially all of the $600-700m annual FCF before growth through 2027 while distributions stay suspended and IDRs stay dormant. Marked back through that waterfall, $1.85bn of EBITDA at 9x supports ~$39/unit but at 7x supports roughly nothing — the equity is a hyper-levered residual on the exit multiple, so the flagged upside is an assumption, not a mechanical SoP, and the FIP rule applies: score the equity, not the event (cap 4). The milestones are genuinely forward and unfired, but they are cash uses on year-level windows rather than a binary re-rate trigger, and 20 months after the January 2025 distribution suspension the recovery is already 40% harvested off the low — real, slow, and mostly priced.
